step1_figure.description: A 6-transistor CMOS Schmitt trigger circuit. Figure 18.4 explicitly shows the bottom (NMOS) portion used to calculate the upper switching point, while the full 6-transistor circuit is implied and simulated in the text.

upper_switching_point_VSPH.description: The input voltage threshold where the output transitions from high to low, initiating positive feedback through M2 and M3.

equation.explanation: Determines the upper switching point based on the transconductance ratio of the input NMOS (M1) and the feedback NMOS (M3).
equation.assumptions: Currents in M1 and M3 are essentially the same at the switching point; body effect increases VTHN2 and VTHN3 equally.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using typical SKY130 NMOS Vth (0.42V) and the W/L ratios provided in the textbook example.

m2_sizing_rule.description: Design rule for sizing the switch transistor M2 relative to M1 and M3.

equation.explanation: Ensures M2 acts effectively as a switch without bottlenecking the pull-down path.
equation.assumptions: Standard digital design practice for series switches.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using Example 18.1 sizing: W2=10, W1=10. beta2 = beta1, which satisfies the >= condition.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on the textbook's recommended sizing strategy.

lower_switching_point_VSPL.description: The input voltage threshold where the output transitions from low to high, initiating positive feedback through the PMOS network.

equation.explanation: Determines the lower switching point based on the transconductance ratio of the input PMOS (M5) and the feedback PMOS (M6).
equation.assumptions: Currents in M5 and M6 are equal at the switching point.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using typical SKY130 PMOS |Vth| (0.42V) and the W/L ratios provided in the textbook example.

propagation_delay_tpHL.description: High-to-low propagation delay time of the Schmitt trigger.

equation.explanation: RC delay of discharging the load capacitance through the series NMOS transistors M1 and M2.
equation.assumptions: Neglects intrinsic output capacitance of the Schmitt trigger itself.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Highly dependent on the actual load capacitance and the effective large-signal resistance during switching.

propagation_delay_tpLH.description: Low-to-high propagation delay time of the Schmitt trigger.

equation.explanation: RC delay of charging the load capacitance through the series PMOS transistors M4 and M5.
equation.assumptions: Neglects intrinsic output capacitance of the Schmitt trigger itself.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Highly dependent on the actual load capacitance and the effective large-signal resistance during switching.

step3_testbench.description: Measures the upper and lower switching points (VSPH, VSPL) using a slow input ramp, and measures propagation delays (tpHL, tpLH) using fast input pulses.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Schmitt Trigger Testbench
.lib ${SKY130_PDK} tt

* Parameters based on Example 18.1
.param W_xm1=10 W_xm2=10 W_xm3=22.5 W_xm4=20 W_xm5=26 W_xm6=20
.param L_xm1=1 L_xm2=1 L_xm3=1 L_xm4=1 L_xm5=1 L_xm6=1

* DUT
xm1 N002 Vin 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
VDD VDD 0 1.8
xm5 N001 Vin VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm5} l={L_xm5}
xm4 Vout Vin N001 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
xm2 Vout Vin N002 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm6 0 Vout N001 VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm6} l={L_xm6}
xm3 VDD Vout N002 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}

* Load capacitance for delay measurement
Cload Vout 0 10f

* Stimulus: Slow ramp (0 to 2us) for hysteresis, then fast pulses (2.1us to 2.2us) for delay
V1 Vin 0 PWL(0 0 1u 1.8 2u 0 2.1u 0 2.101u 1.8 2.2u 1.8 2.201u 0)

.control
* Run transient analysis with fine resolution
tran 10p 2.3u

* Measure VSPH (Vin rising, Vout falls during the first 1us)
meas tran vsph find v(Vin) when v(Vout)=0.9 fall=1

* Measure VSPL (Vin falling, Vout rises between 1us and 2us)
meas tran vspl find v(Vin) when v(Vout)=0.9 rise=1

* Measure tpHL (Vin fast rise at 2.1u, Vout fast fall)
meas tran t_phl trig v(Vin) val=0.9 rise=2 targ v(Vout) val=0.9 fall=2

* Measure tpLH (Vin fast fall at 2.2u, Vout fast rise)
meas tran t_plh trig v(Vin) val=0.9 fall=2 targ v(Vout) val=0.9 rise=2

print vsph vspl t_phl t_plh
quit
.endc
.end
